Q: Are the usize/isize types in Rust guaranteed to always be either 32 or 64 bits? A:

is it guaranteed (via a specification, RFC, or otherwise) to always return 4 or 8?

No.

Values of 2, 4 and 8 exist in official ports, there is also an unofficial port to cheri, where I believe it has a value of 16.

A value of 1 seems implausible, it has been argued that C99 requires a value of at least 2, and a system with only 256 bytes of usable ram would probably not be a very attractive target for a language as high-level as rust anyway.

If I compile a program targeting a 16 bit architecture, will std::mem::size_of::() return 2

The term "16 bit architecture" is somewhat ambiguous.

usize in rust is defined to be "pointer sized". This differs from size_t in C which is defined based on the maximum size of data structures.

There do exist some architectures where both the pointer size and the data size are 16-bits, for example the TI MSP430 microcontrollers but most systems that were marketed as "16-bit" had a total address space that was larger than 16 bits. Similarly most systems that were marketed as 8-bit had a total address space that was large than 8 bits.

If rust were to be ported to 16-bit x86 then the size of "usize" would depend on the "memory model" used. The tiny and small memory models have 16-bit pointers, so usize would be 2 bytes in size. The large and huge models have 32-bit pointers, so usize would be 4 bytes in size.

The "medium" and "compact" models raise an interesting question. Under these memory models code pointers have a different size to data pointers. If a rust compiler were to support those memory models then someone would have to make a judgement call as to what "pointer sized" meant.

Q: Vista CPRS CONNECTion WITh MIRTH AND THEN USING MIRTH I WANT TO GET SELECTED PATIENT DATA FROM CPRS A:

CPRS doesn't do HL7 export! It's just the clinical GUI. HL7 generation happens at the VistA/Cache level (HL7 package), configured by a system manager, not something you trigger from CPRS's print option. This isn't a CPRS feature, it's VistA system-level interface setup - you'll need someone with system manager access to configure it.
